newsitem.title: USA: PG&E expects storm to hit N. Calif. on Sat.
newsitem.headline: PG&E expects storm to hit N. Calif. on Sat.

text.p: San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric Co (PG&E) said Friday it expected a heavy storm system to hit its northern California service territory Saturday night.

Meteorologists said that the storm will bring heavy rains, as much as ten inches of precipitation between Sunday and next Tuesday in the Santa Cruz Mountains and areas along the Russian River, the utility reported.
PG&E said it is getting ready to respond to any power outages caused by the weather front and has put damage assessment and repair crews on alert.
"Already this winter, Northern and Central California have seen several storms that have brought heavy rains and high winds," said Bob Gross, manager of PG&E's Operations Coordination Center.

Although PG&E has sharply expanded its tree trimming efforts, Gross noted that the abundance of precipitation to date has left the ground soft in many areas which makes trees more susceptible to falling over in moderate to strong winds.
